manufacturer_data.description: Ember BLE manufacturer data under Bluetooth SIG company ID 0x03C1.

discovery_patterns: Home Assistant bluetooth manifest: local_name `Ember C*` + manufacturer_id 961.
Home Assistant bluetooth manifest: local_name `Ember T*` + manufacturer_id 961.
manufacturer_data.payload_notes: python-ember-mug treats short (<4 byte) payloads as a signed model/color byte and longer payloads as bytes 1..3 = model_id, generation, colour_id. Known model_id/generation mapping includes Mug 1/2, Travel Mug, Cup, and Tumbler; color IDs map to black/white/red/copper/rose gold/stainless steel/sandstone/sage green/grey/blue/gold. The exact manufacturer-data binary contract remains inferred from public library behavior.

device.name: Ember Mug
device.notes:
Covers Ember Mug 2 (10/14 oz), Travel Mug 2/2+, Cup (6 oz), Tumbler (16 oz). Official Android app package is `com.embertech`; APKPure XAPK inspected: Ember app 4.5.9 / versionCode 220. The decompiled Android manifest confirms BLE permissions, package `com.embertech`, and Nordic DFU services; Flutter AOT strings expose the Ember Bluetooth model names and characteristic helper names such as `characteristicForTargetTemperature`, `characteristicForLED`, `characteristicForPushEvent`, `characteristicForDSK`, and `ManufacturerDataX|get#emberAdvertisementInfoOrNull`.
All protocol UUIDs use template fc54XXXX-236c-4c94-8fa9-944a3e5353fa. Standard Mug/Cup/Tumbler service is fc543622. Travel Mug libraries also use fc543621 and fc5421a1 as service UUIDs. BLE SIG company ID is 0x03C1 (961). Home Assistant discovery matches local names `Ember C*` and `Ember T*` with manufacturer_id 961, plus the known service UUIDs.
Pairing/auth: public libraries can connect locally with BLE pairing, but writes may fail until the product has first been set up in the official app. python-ember-mug models DSK (read) and UDSK (read/write, base64-encoded string); its `make_writable()` helper attempts to write a random UDSK if the mug is not writable. Treat UDSK/DSK details as partially understood.
Temperature values are little-endian uint16 centi-degrees C. Target 0x0000 disables temperature control. python-ember-mug enforces setpoint bounds of 49-63 C or 120-145 F. Liquid level is a raw 0-30-ish value; orlopau notes it may only update on charger and only 0/30 are app-significant. Push event notifications are one-byte event IDs and should prompt clients to re-read the affected characteristic.
Device coverage is wider than the original orlopau Ember Mug 2 docs: sopelj/python-ember-mug reports tested Mug, Mug 2, Cup, Tumbler, Travel Mug, and Travel Mug 2 support. No dedicated ESPHome Ember component was found; the Home Assistant integration works through BLE adapters or active ESPHome Bluetooth proxies.
Schema gaps (device-specs/schema.json intentionally not modified): there is no dedicated field for BLE manufacturer-data format, characteristic endianness, write authentication/pairing caveats, multiple equivalent service UUIDs sharing one characteristic table, or per-field evidence links. These are documented in notes and references. (Enum/value maps and unit/scale, formerly on this list, are now first-class: format fields carry `values`, `unit` and `scale` — see $defs/number_semantics in the schema.)

issued_to_client: DSK read from the mug, and the UDSK the client wrote

factory_reset.effect: Clears the stored claim and returns the mug to pairing mode; temperature history and target are lost.

procedures.indicator: LED changes colour and the mug re-enters pairing mode.
procedures.name: Base button held

steps.action: Press and hold the button on the base of the mug until the LED changes.
steps.notes: Hold time varies by model; watch the LED rather than the clock.

ble.pin_source: None — claiming is a characteristic write, not a BLE PIN pairing.

methods.description: Scan, connect, then claim write access. Temperature reads work immediately; setpoint and LED writes may not.

steps.action: Put the mug in pairing mode by holding the button on the base until the LED shows the pairing colour.
steps.expect: Mug advertises with local name Ember* and manufacturer ID 961 (0x03C1).

steps.action: Connect and read the device state characteristics to confirm the link.
If writes are rejected, claim the mug by writing a UDSK value.
steps.notes: python-ember-mug's make_writable() writes a random UDSK. Treat the DSK/UDSK semantics as partially understood; keep the value you wrote, since it is the client's claim on the mug.

setup.notes: There is nothing to provision — no network, no account, no cloud. Ember support confirms the mug even works with no client at all: unpaired it holds a fixed 135 F (~57 C) default target, inside the 49-63 C settable range. What trips clients up instead is write authorization: several libraries report that a mug fresh out of the box accepts reads but rejects writes until a client has claimed it by writing the UDSK characteristic (what python-ember-mug calls making the mug writable). Historically that first claim was done by the vendor app.

rejoin.notes: The usual symptom of a mug that will not connect is not a broken claim but a phone that is still holding the single allowed connection. Close or uninstall the other client, or power-cycle the mug on its coaster, before assuming a reset is required.

characteristics.name: Mug Name
characteristics.notes: orlopau documents up to 14 bytes ASCII without spaces; python-ember-mug accepts UTF-8 writes matching a 1-16 character restricted regex. Cup/Tumbler are modeled as not supporting name; Travel Mug is read-only in python-ember-mug's README table.

format.name: current_temp_raw
format.notes: Wire unit is always centi-°C regardless of the display unit selected via fc540004 — that characteristic changes what the mug and app show, not what is encoded here.

characteristics.name: Current Temperature
characteristics.notes: Little-endian uint16; value * 0.01 = degrees C.

set_target_temp.description: Set target temperature (value * 0.01 = degrees C; 0x0000 disables heater)

temp_high.description: High byte of the same little-endian centi-°C value; 0x0000 across both bytes disables temperature control.

temp_low.description: Low byte of the little-endian uint16 target in centi-°C. The pair encodes round(target_c * 100): 56.5 C -> 5650 -> temp_low 0x12, temp_high 0x16. Wire unit is °C even when the display unit (fc540004) is Fahrenheit.

format.name: target_temp_raw
format.notes: 0x0000 means temperature control disabled, not 0 °C. Nonzero setpoints are accepted in 49-63 °C (120-145 °F converted to centi-°C before writing).

characteristics.name: Target Temperature
characteristics.notes: Little-endian uint16 centi-degrees C. 0x0000 disables heater/temp control. python-ember-mug accepts nonzero setpoints only in 49-63 C or 120-145 F, converting F to device C before writing.

format.name: temp_unit
format.notes: Display preference only — every temperature characteristic stays centi-°C on the wire whatever this byte says.

characteristics.name: Temperature Unit
characteristics.notes: 0 = Celsius, 1 = Fahrenheit; affects device/app display unit, not raw temp encoding.

characteristics.name: Liquid Level
characteristics.notes: Raw one-byte level. orlopau observed 0 = empty and 30 = not empty; the app appears to ignore intermediate values. python-ember-mug formats it as raw / 30 * 100 percent.

set_time.description: Set device clock (4-byte Unix timestamp LE + 1-byte timezone offset)

characteristics.name: Date Time Zone
characteristics.notes: orlopau calls this a write-only sink using 4-byte little-endian Unix timestamp plus one timezone-offset byte. python-ember-mug currently reads it as a 4-byte big-endian timestamp and does not write it in the normal update path, so endianness/readability are uncertain.

characteristics.name: Battery
characteristics.notes: orlopau documents a 5-byte value: byte 0 battery percent (5-100, not scaled), byte 1 charging status, bytes 2-3 battery temperature as little-endian centi-degrees C, byte 4 legacy/probable voltage. Current python-ember-mug only exposes percent and charging-base boolean.

characteristics.name: Liquid State
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug maps 0=standby, 1=empty, 2=filling, 3=cold/no-temp-control, 4=cooling, 5=heating, 6=target/perfect, 7=warm/no-temp-control. orlopau's older app notes saw 3 as emitted but not registered by the app.

set_volume_high.description: Set Travel Mug beep volume to high

set_volume_low.description: Set Travel Mug beep volume to low

set_volume_medium.description: Set Travel Mug beep volume to medium

characteristics.name: Volume
characteristics.notes: Travel Mug button-beep volume in python-ember-mug. Values: 0=low, 1=medium, 2=high. Marked N/A for Mug/Cup/Tumbler.

characteristics.name: Last Location
characteristics.notes: Present in python-ember-mug's MugCharacteristic enum as LAST_LOCATION (write). Payload format was not found in public docs or light app static inspection.

characteristics.name: Acceleration
characteristics.notes: Present in python-ember-mug's MugCharacteristic enum as UUID_ACCELERATION with comment "Unsure what it does"; payload format unknown.

characteristics.name: Firmware
characteristics.notes: orlopau documents 4-6 bytes: firmware version, hardware version, and optional bootloader version, each little-endian uint16. python-ember-mug exposes all three fields.

characteristics.name: Mug ID
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug reads this as 6 bytes mug_id followed by serial number from byte 7 onward. The mug_id decoding is marked uncertain in the library.

characteristics.name: DSK
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug calls this a unique ID used for auth in the app and base64-encodes/decodes the byte string. Exact auth semantics unknown.

set_udsk.description: Write app auth/user DSK material; exact semantics uncertain

characteristics.name: UDSK
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug calls this UDSK, used for auth in the app. It treats all-zero 20-byte reads as missing and attempts to write a base64-encoded random string in `make_writable()` when normal writes fail.

characteristics.name: Control Register Address
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug enum comment says "int/temp lock - Address". App AOT strings include `characteristicForControlRegisterAddress`. Payload and temp-lock behavior remain uncertain.

characteristics.name: Control Register Data
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug enum comment says battery charge info read/write; for Travel Mug it reads the first byte as battery voltage/state. App AOT strings include `characteristicForControlRegisterData`. Exact register map is unknown.

characteristics.name: Push Event
characteristics.notes: One-byte notification event ID. python-ember-mug maps 1=battery changed, 2=charger connected, 3=charger disconnected, 4=target temp changed, 5=drink temp changed, 6=auth info not found, 7=liquid level changed, 8=liquid state changed, 9=battery voltage state changed. Clients should re-read the affected characteristic.

characteristics.name: Statistics
characteristics.notes: python-ember-mug subscribes only when debug is enabled and logs raw bytes as statistics; payload format was not found.

characteristics.name: LED Color
characteristics.notes: LED color characteristic. orlopau documents the byte order as red, blue, green, alpha. python-ember-mug's Colour tuple and app log strings label writes as R/G/B/brightness. Existing integrations appear to use [red, green, blue, brightness]; verify on hardware if precise blue/green ordering matters.

services.name: Ember Mug Service
services.notes: Standard Mug/Cup/Tumbler service. Travel Mug variants use service UUIDs fc543621-236c-4c94-8fa9-944a3e5353fa and fc5421a1-236c-4c94-8fa9-944a3e5353fa with the same fc54XXXX characteristic UUID pattern according to python-ember-mug. Schema has no way to declare equivalent service UUIDs without duplicating every characteristic.
